findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it never guards the attribute
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only honours conditional methods named `include_<attr>?`. The method defined here is `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — including as `null` for every user who has no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and note that it then also needs to respect the untrusted-attribute rules, see the separate finding).

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking a TL0 user's website to anonymous viewers
findings.body: `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111) deliberately hides `website` (among others) when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true — i.e. a trust-level-0 user's profile seen by an anonymous visitor — as a spam mitigation. The new `website_name` attribute is declared as a plain attribute and is therefore always serialized, exposing the host (and, for same-domain cases, the full path) of a TL0 user's website to anonymous visitors. The template renders `model.website_name` as the visible text, so the spam URL becomes visible again even though `model.website` is suppressed. Add `website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or gate it on the same condition).

findings.title: `"." << website_host` mutates a string literal in place
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because the literal is a fresh unfrozen object on each evaluation, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment `# frozen_string_literal: true` is added to this file (or the global frozen-literal option is enabled). Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

findings.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case websites fall through to the host-only branch
findings.body: `URI("http://Example.com/user").host` returns `"Example.com"` with the original casing, while `Discourse.current_hostname` is normally lowercase. The equality check on line 141 and the sibling-subdomain comparison on line 146 therefore fail for a user who typed their own domain with capitals, and the full path is not shown even though the domains match. Downcase both hosts before comparing.

findings.title: Only `URI#path` is appended, dropping query and fragment from the displayed URL
findings.body: For same-domain websites the display string is `host + URI(...).path`, which silently discards any query string or fragment (e.g. `http://example.com/u?id=1` is shown as `example.com/u`). Since the whole point of this change is to show the complete URL when the domain matches the instance domain, the link text can now differ from the actual `href`. Consider using the request-URI (path + query) or the full URL minus the scheme.

findings.title: No test coverage for the sibling-subdomain branch, for non-parsable websites, or for the TL0/anonymous case
findings.body: The three new examples only cover the `==` branch and the `ends_with?` branch. Uncovered behaviours that the implementation makes non-trivial claims about: (1) the `elsif` sibling-subdomain branch (`www.example.com` website with a `forum.example.com` instance) which the inline comment advertises; (2) a website stored without a scheme or otherwise unparsable, where `URI(...).host` is nil and `website_name` becomes nil so the website disappears from the profile entirely; (3) the "TL0 user seen as anonymous" context at the top of this file, which asserts `website` is hidden but does not assert anything about `website_name` — exactly the attribute that currently leaks.
